Chicago, IL, USA University of Illinois - Chicago



Director of Administrative Operations - Department of Dermatology

Hiring Department: Department of Dermatology

Location: Chicago, IL USA

Requisition ID: 1042695

Posting Close Date: 11/18/2026

Salary: The salary range for the position is $120,000 - 140,000. Salary is competitive and commensurate with qualifications and experience, while also considering internal equity.

About the University of Illinois Chicago

UIC is among the nation's preeminent urban public research universities, a Carnegie RU/VH research institution, and the largest university in Chicago. UIC serves over 34,000 students, comprising one of the most diverse student bodies in the nation and is designated as a Minority Serving Institution (MSI), an Asian American and Native American Pacific Islander Serving Institution (AANAPSI) and a Hispanic Serving Institution (HSI). Through its 16 colleges, UIC produces nationally and internationally recognized multidisciplinary academic programs in concert with civic, corporate and community partners worldwide, including a full complement of health sciences colleges. By emphasizing cutting-edge and transformational research along with a commitment to the success of all students, UIC embodies the dynamic, vibrant and engaged urban university. Recent "Best Colleges" rankings published by U.S. News & World Report, found UIC climbed up in its rankings among top public schools in the nation and among all national universities. UIC has over 300,000 alumni, and is one of the largest employers in the city of Chicago.

This position is intended to be eligible for benefits. This includes Health, Dental, Vision, Life Insurance, a Retirement Plan, Paid time Off, and Tuition waivers for employees and dependents.

The Department of Dermatology at the University of Illinois Chicago is seeking a Director of Administrative Operations.

Position Summary:

Under minimal supervision oversees the operational, financial, regulatory, and business activities of the unit. This includes financial analysis and strategy related to medical service, health maintenance, and procurement programs; human resource and facilities management; business development, marketing, and public relations; contract negotiations; interfacing and ensuring compliance with granting organizations, regulatory agencies, university policies, and procedures. Represents Department Head on campus/university committees.

Duties & Responsibilities:

Financial Management / Business Development:

Develop the annual budget, including providing monthly financial reporting and forecasting, cash flow management, capital spending and expenditures review and approval.

Develop strategic plans, annual goals and objectives and administrative direction of the unit.

Identify new business opportunities by analyzing and presenting financial data for the development of new services, facilities, procedures, and costs.

Oversee the operational payment structure, monitor payments and patient billing as outlined in contracts and ensure compliance with insurance companies.

Lead departmental marketing efforts by developing and implementing a marketing plan and measuring and reporting results.

Create, implement, and monitor departmental strategic plan.

Coordinates maintenance, repair, remodeling, and equipment purchases by identifying needs, planning, budgeting, and reviewing contracts as needed.

Operations Management:

Manage off-site practices, once established, by negotiating the terms for revenue generating contracts, monitoring, and renegotiating leases.

Direct all day-to-day administrative activities.

Maintain and report space utilization inventory.

Manage grant activities (pre and post award, extramural) including review and submission of grant and contract proposals; creates and maintains documentation of expenditures, reports, proposal submissions, and awards.

Grants Management:

Collaborates closely with OVCR to ensure proper grant management.

Recruit, select, evaluate, and train administrative staff.

Human Resources:

Oversee and direct recruitment activities of faculty, physicians, and staff with assistance of appropriate management staff. Ensure appropriate credentials are received as needed.

Develop and monitor compensation plans, income guarantees and productivity incentives.

Performs other related duties and participate in special projects as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor's degree in Healthcare Administration, Business Administration, Management or in a related field.

A minimum of 5 years of administrative/management experience.

Strong interpersonal, management and communication skills. Knowledge of Microsoft Office.

Preferred Qualifications:

Master's degree preferred.

Management experience in healthcare environment desired.

The University of Illinois System is an equal opportunity employer, including but not limited to disability and/or veteran status, and complies with all applicable state and federal employment mandates. Please visit Required Employment Notices and Posters to view our non-discrimination statement and find additional information about required background checks, sexual harassment/misconduct disclosures, and employment eligibility review through E-Verify.

The university provides accommodations to applicants and employees. Request an Accommodation

title: Assistant Professor in Quantum Computing and Quantum Engineering (Position # 50155)
description:
Dallas Southern Methodist University, Lyle School of Engineering

The Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering (ECE) at Southern Methodist University (SMU) invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor position in Quantum Computing and Quantum Engineering. We seek outstanding candidates who will establish a high-impact, externally funded research program, contribute to the growing quantum ecosystem at SMU, and help shape the future of quantum engineering education and research. 

We welcome applicants working broadly in quantum computing and quantum engineering, including areas such as quantum architecture and systems, hardware-software co-design, quantum design automation, quantum error correction, quantum security, quantum sensing, and quantum communications. Candidates whose research connects quantum computing with areas such as computer architecture, hardware and systems security, and electronic design automation (EDA) are particularly encouraged to apply. Exceptional candidates from other areas of electrical and computer engineering with a demonstrated record of research excellence are also encouraged to apply. 

The successful candidate will be expected to establish a nationally recognized research program, attract external funding, advise graduate and undergraduate students, and develop interdisciplinary collaborations within and beyond SMU. The candidate will contribute to undergraduate and graduate teaching in Quantum Engineering and related ECE areas, including courses in quantum computing, quantum sensing, quantum communications and networking, quantum design automation, and other emerging quantum technologies. 

The position offers opportunities to contribute to and collaborate with SMU's growing quantum computing ecosystem, including the M.S. in Quantum Engineering program and the Darwin Deason Institute for Cybersecurity. 

About the Lyle School of Engineering 

The Lyle School of Engineering has embarked on an ambitious journey, successfully hiring numerous outstanding faculty members, including several endowed professors during the recent past. Our culture of faculty growth thrives on innovation, fostering a dynamic and collaborative environment. We are committed to cutting-edge research funded by competitive federal grants, industry-funded projects and philanthropic gifts, which advances our academic goals and provides students with a competitive edge in industry and/or academia. Our mission is to lead in the digital transformation of engineering education, equipping students with cutting-edge knowledge and skills to emerge as confident, capable leaders. Through excellence and innovation, we aim to significantly impact the engineering landscape and beyond.  Lyle offers a collaborative research environment with growing strengths in quantum information science and engineering, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, advanced computing, energy systems, and semiconductor technologies and provides strong opportunities for academic, industry and government collaboration.

About SMU 

SMU is a private university of 12,000 students and offers strong undergraduate, graduate and professional programs through eight schools – Dedman College of Humanities and Sciences, Cox School of Business, Meadows School of the Arts, Lyle School of Engineering, Perkins School of Theology, Dedman School of Law, Simmons School of Education and Human Development, and the Moody Graduate School of Advanced Studies. SMU is a Carnegie R1 research university, a designation recognizing the highest level of research activity. The university continues to invest in expanding its research capabilities and supporting interdisciplinary scholarships. It offers a collaborative research environment with growing strengths in quantum information science and engineering, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, advanced computing, and semiconductor technologies. Located in Dallas, Texas, SMU provides strong opportunities for academic, industry, and government collaboration. 

SMU is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, sexual orientation, or gender identity and expression.

title: Head Women’s Soccer Coach
description:
500 W University St, Shawnee, OK, USA Oklahoma Baptist University

OBU Mission Statement

OBU transforms lives by equipping students to pursue academic excellence, integrate faith with all areas of knowledge, engage a diverse world, and live worthy of the high calling of God in Christ.

 

Expectations for all Employees

Oklahoma Baptist University achieves its mission through a shared commitment to the following expectations.  All employees must embrace these expectations and model them in their behavior.

  • Demonstrate commitment to the essentials of the Christian faith.
  • Commit to the mission and vision of Oklahoma Baptist University.
  • Treat people with dignity and respect.
  • Build relationships on honesty, integrity, and trust.
  • Strive for excellence through teamwork, leadership, and a strong work ethic.
  • Manage human and financial resources wisely and efficiently.

Purpose: The Head Women’s Soccer Coach requires all functions normally associated with an intercollegiate athletics program in women’s soccer and will be bound by the university/athletic department mission statement listed above.

 

Essential Functions:

·        Recruit unique students to the university to participate in varsity women’s soccer.

·        Coaching and management of all practice sessions.

·        Adhere to NCAA, Conference, and University regulations regarding recruiting, admissions standards, and eligibility.

·        Monitor the team’s academic performance.

·        Scheduling competitions and related events.

·        Budget management and organization.

·        Purchase and maintain equipment and supplies.

·        Event preparations.

·        Campus and community relations.

·        Marketing and developing of the program.

·        Fundraising for the program.

·         Supervision of coaches and volunteers.

 

Other Duties:

·         Other duties as assigned by the Director of Athletics.

 

Required Qualifications:

·        Collegiate level participation in soccer is preferred.

·        Ability to recruit unique students for the women’s soccer program.

·        Good communication skills.

Education:

Required: Bachelor’s degree

Preferred: Master’s degree

 

Experience:

Required: Collegiate or High School level experience coaching women’s soccer.

Preferred: Collegiate level experience coaching women’s soccer.

 

Equipment:

·         Must be able to drive a 15-passenger van.

 

Physical Requirements:

·        Must be able to demonstrate soccer techniques for coaching purposes.

 

Special Requirements:

·         Must be a member of a local evangelical* Christian church.

*Evangelical is a broad term referring to segment within Christianity which maintains the authority of the Bible and the belief in salvation by faith in Jesus alone.

·         Please apply using the link for “Administrative Applications” on the OBU website at: https://www.okbu.edu/hr/jobs.html

 

OBU Benefits Summary:

OBU understands that our employees are our most valuable assets when fulfilling our mission. We strive to offer an extensive array of benefits and opportunities for employees to choose from. Full-time employees benefit from the generous OBU provision of premium contributions for nationwide family-friendly Health and Dental coverages along with free life insurance that includes accidental death and dismemberment equal to an employee’s base salary. OBU provides access to optional employee-paid ancillary benefits like vision, hospitalization, critical illness, accident, additional employee-paid family life insurance coverages, and education benefits at OBU and other institutions of higher education. There is generous paid time off that includes annual granted vacation time, accrued sick leave, six annual holidays, and week-long breaks for Thanksgiving and Christmas that include energy conservation days. For all employees working at least half-time, there is an employer matching opportunity for retirement investments in a 403(b)(9) plan administered by Guide Stone. There are numerous other perks and opportunities for OBU employees including FREE family membership to the OBU Recreation and Wellness Center or RAWC, Global outreach university mission trips, cafeteria discounts, and parking privileges to name a few. For more information about the current OBU employee benefits and opportunities, please contact the Human Resources staff at HR@okbu.edu.
